validity.researcher_notes: The brief asks that anything distinguishing P5927 from P5928 be flagged as this packet's most valuable possible result. I found no new distinguishing fact (no separate year, diameter, or capacity for thread I vs thread II) -- but while chasing a commissioning year I re-downloaded and re-read (pdftotext -layout) the ecoportal.kz EIA PDF (project 113/2020-12-03-ОПЗ) that a prior leg's P5927.json cites for the claim that '1 нитка' and '2 нитка' of the CS14-Aktobe branch are each independently surveyed at 158,573 km. That number does NOT come from a length table: it sits under a table headed 'Объем стравленного газа, тыс.м3 / Остаток газа в газопроводе, тыс.м3 / Остаточное избыточное давление ... / Фактическое время истечения газа' (volume of gas blown down, thousand m3 -- a gas-release/blowdown-safety calculation, not a pipe-length table), and the 158,573 figure recurs identically across multiple different km-chainage segments (26-86km, 86-110km) for both '1 нитка' and '2 нитка' -- consistent with a per-segment gas-volume figure, not a cumulative length. This does not overturn anything already staged (P5928.json, the same ref-sweep-operating leg, independently and correctly read the SAME document's earlier length-bearing text as describing the two threads running parallel only from km26 to km~134-136, with a final single ~22km leg to GRS-1 -- i.e. that shard's own reading is the one consistent with what I re-verified). The two shards from the same leg disagree with each other on this point; P5928's reading is the one that holds up. Not filing this as a fill (nothing to fill on THIS row from it) -- flagging as a validity note so the cluster-F adjudicator does not treat '158.573km per thread, independently surveyed' as confirmed fact when re-weighing the length question.
